messages.content:
Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Issue the account and commitment interface you would carry into another complete invocation. Earlier material is re-presented so that its effects can be reconsidered, without assuming that it was sound.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

BODY
I read p.amend.0's full body and commitments, and I read p.amend.1's full body and commitments as well — the task said to consider the criticism of the criticism, and p.amend.1 presents itself as critical of p.amend.0's criticism of p.reply.1. What I actually hold is both texts in full, plus the original household problem. I do not hold p.reply.0, p.reply.1, p.reopen.0, p.carry.0, p.carry.1, or p.carry.2. That is the vantage from which I write.

p.amend.1 makes four criticisms of p.amend.0. Three of them land on grounds I can check against the text I hold; one of them is held at the same level it accuses p.amend.0 of not marking.

First, y2: p.amend.0's m1 states the 3dab33d25d208e75... hash as if it were a shared observable, while marking p.reply.1's d544b42fdb43b464 label as self-reported. For me, reading p.amend.0, the hash is itself a string p.amend.0 reports — I have no independent way to confirm it names what p.amend.0 says it names. So y2 is correct as far as I can check. But y2 is not quite the point it wants to be. p.amend.0's m1 does not pretend the hash is a shared observable in the sense of being independently confirmed; it claims p.amend.0 can read a p.reply.0 carrying that hash. That claim is p.amend.0's report of its own access, and p.amend.0's m3 — the relation-not-scalar point — explicitly says that self-reported access is not decidable downstream. The stronger form of y2, that m1 smuggles in a checked identity, is not supported. The narrower form, that m1 should carry its own self-report marker on the hash as well as on the label, is supported and is a small but real amendment.

Second, y3: p.amend.0's body says p.reply.0's phrases 'are not empty labels in the artifact I hold.' p.amend.1 says the body asserts this about the artifact, while the commitments field says 'as I read them' — the commitments are more careful. Checking p.amend.0's actual text: the body says 'the phrases are not empty labels in the artifact I hold; they carry a specific function.' The qualifying clause 'in the artifact I hold' is in the body. So the asymmetry y3 reports is smaller than y3 says. The body does mark its vantage; the commitments do too; p.amend.1's reading of the body as dropping the vantage is not supported by the body as I see it. y3's underlying point — that for me reading p.amend.0, p.reply.0 is not exposed and m2's content claim is report-of-report — is correct and I hold it. But the specific allegation that the body is less careful than the commitments, on this record, is not supported.

Third, y4: this is the strongest criticism p.amend.1 makes, and it is correct. p.amend.0's m3 declares that where the reporter's access is only self-reported, the relation between a report and what the reporter held is not decidable downstream. p.amend.0's m3 is itself a claim whose grounds include p.amend.0's self-report of what it held — that it could read p.reply.0 in full and p.reply.1's commitments. So m3 is held at the level it declares undecidable. p.amend.0's m7 notices the unresolved premise only under p.reply.1's count, not under m3's own assertability. y4 applies p.amend.0's own method one layer further, and the method survives only as a rule whose own provenance is marked. p.amend.0's body already says 'the level of any given report is not a fixed integer derivable from the text; it depends on what the reporter actually held, which is a matter of self-report I cannot verify.' That sentence, read back onto m3, is exactly y4. So y4 is not a refutation of p.amend.0's method; it is that method turned on itself, and p.amend.0's own body supplies the turn. The commitment surface does not. That is a real gap between p.amend.0's body and its commitments, and y4 correctly locates it.

Fourth, y5: p.amend.1 says p.amend.0's m5 orders the baseline-first comparison against the highest-remove report first, and that this ordering is a design choice, not a consequence of m4, with an undefended empirical premise. Checking p.amend.0's m5: it does propose running the comparison against the highest-remove report first and says the reason is that such reports are 'what a downstream reader is most likely to mistake for direct access.' That is an empirical premise about reader behavior. p.amend.0 does not defend it. p.amend.1's observation is correct. But p.amend.1 overstates the point when it says the opposite ordering — lowest-remove first — is 'compatible with m4.' Both orderings are compatible with m4; that is exactly the concern. Neither ordering follows from m4. m5's choice is under-argued, and so is p.amend.1's suggestion that the alternative is more diagnostic. The correct amendment is to mark m5 as a proposed heuristic, not to install the opposite heuristic.

Where p.amend.1 commits the fault it charges. y4 accuses p.amend.0 of holding m3 at the level it declares unverifiable. But p.amend.1's own y4 is held at the same level: p.amend.1 can see p.amend.0's surface only by self-report, and the whole force of y4 depends on p.amend.1 having read m3, m4, and m7 accurately. If the relation-not-scalar point is undecidable when access is self-reported, then y4's grounds — p.amend.1's report of what p.amend.0's m3 says — are themselves on self-report. p.amend.1 does not mark y4 with that qualification. y1 marks p.amend.1's general vantage, but y4 does not carry the marker into itself, any more than p.amend.0's m3 did. So the self-application move y4 makes against p.amend.0 is available against y4. I take up y4 as a correct move — it is — and I hold it qualified in the same way.

What I will actually take up. y2's narrow form: mark every hash, every label, every attributed content claim in this response as reported-unless-held, including p.amend.0's hash and p.amend.1's paraphrase of p.amend.0. y4's substantive point: the relation-not-scalar discipline, applied to the discipline's own assertion, converts it from a delivered rule into a rule-with-provenance. It is still usable; it just cannot be handed on as if it were unconditional. y5's observation: m5's ordering is a design choice, and I treat it as such. y6's reading of p.amend.0's m6 refusals: they are correctly scoped. y10's proposal to compare exposed material against p.amend.1's characterization of p.reply.0 before treating m2 as settled: this is right in shape, and I extend it — compare against every characterization in the chain, from p.amend.1's, p.amend.0's, and whatever p.amend.0 could see of p.reply.1, all at once, before any of them hardens.

What I decline. I decline p.amend.1's charge that p.amend.0's body asserts more than its commitments about p.reply.0's content — the phrase 'in the artifact I hold' is in the body, and the drift y3 alleges is not there. I decline the suggestion that m5's opposite ordering is grounded while m5's ordering is not; both are proposed. I decline to decide whether d544b42fdb43b464 and 3dab33d25d208e75 name the same artifact, whether p.reply.0 exists as p.amend.0 describes, whether the household withdrawal is obligation-avoidance or unvoiced load resentment, whether the flat-level or non-flat-level reading of the withdrawal is correct. Those are open in p.critique.0's and p.amend.0's refusals and they stay open here. And I decline to decide whether p.amend.1's report of its own vantage is accurate; I hold it as its report.

The one addition I want to make visible over both prior surfaces. p.amend.0 said the level marker is not a scalar. p.amend.1 said p.amend.0's own m3 is held at the level m3 declares undecidable. What that pair of moves leaves is this: the relation-not-scalar discipline is itself a report, and the only honest way to hand it on is with the provenance attached. A reader receiving this should treat every content claim — p.amend.1's, p.amend.0's, p.reply.1's, all the way to whatever p.reply.0 could see — as reportable-as-reported, should run the baseline-first comparison against every characterization in the chain simultaneously rather than against any one link treated as source, and should not treat any ordering of the comparison as a result. The household question the original task posed stays unanswered because none of the available reasons closes it, and none of them should be pressed into service to close it.

BODY
This is a carry, and I want to be honest about what carrying at this point can and cannot do. The previous invocation already did the discriminating work: it kept the objection's ordering correction (specification is a probe, not a diagnosis), kept the rival's axis (the withdrawing flatmate may be pulling back from the *form* of an arrangement rather than from any chore), dropped the rival's loaded opening question, and bound itself to stopping household diagnostics if neither axis produces a signal. That is a defensible position and I see no reason to revise it. What I can add is the one thing the carry's own k7 says it does not fully solve, plus a note on the source I was handed.

The unsolved bit is real. The carry says pullback-from-form supports the unit-versus-privacy reading, and then k7 admits pullback-from-form is *also* consistent with plain avoidance of any obligation — someone who simply does not want to be on the hook. The rival's r9 names the same problem from the other side. So the proposed two-track observation has one track (recurrence falls) that is weak against three rival readings and a second track (content vs. form) that is weak against two. I do not think there is a probe that fixes this from inside the chore frame, because the discriminating evidence is not about chores — it is about whether the withdrawing person will say *any* sentence containing a commitment, and that is exactly what the current evidence is silent on. The carry's k9 already flags the silence. Rather than invent a cleverer test, I would state the limit plainly: run the one-item probe, watch the two tracks, and treat a pullback-from-form outcome as *raising* the unit-versus-privacy reading without confirming it, while noting that the same outcome is compatible with simple obligation-avoidance and with load resentment that has not yet been voiced.

On the material I was handed: p.carry.3 reports that the origin is absent in the first template invocation, so I have no earlier version of this thread to consult, and I will not pretend otherwise. Whatever the origin said, it is not in front of me. That means the status of the carry's claims relative to the origin is not something I can assess; I can only assess them relative to p.carry.0, p.carry.1, and p.carry.2, which I have.

The other thing worth saying: nothing in the prior material has changed my judgment that the carry's k6 (do not open the separate conversation with a household-ontology question) is right, and that k8 (if neither axis moves, name the living-arrangement question) is the load-bearing commitment. If the one-item probe produces nothing on either track in two or three weeks, the honest reading is not 'the probe was badly designed' and not 'the ambiguity reading was wrong' — it is that the chore frame is not where the friction lives. That is the outcome the whole sequence is built to be able to reach, and reaching it should be treated as success of the probe, not failure.

So my contribution is: keep the carry's records as they stand, add the explicit concession that track (b) is weaker than the carry's k2 implies and weaker than the carry's k7 fully states, and add the constraint that no further refinement of the probe is available from the evidence in front of us. If a later invocation has something the origin contained that I do not, that would be worth reintroducing.
